title: This Larva Digs a Sand Trap and Sucks Its Prey Dry

scenes.text: This insect digs a pit that no ant can climb out of.
It's an antlion larva. It walks backward in circles, flicking sand until the hole is a cone.
Then it buries itself at the bottom, with only its jaws showing.
An ant slips in. The larva flicks sand, and the walls collapse.
It stabs the ant, drinks the insides, and tosses out the shell.
And it can wait months between meals. A hole no ant can climb out of.

description:
The antlion larva digs a cone-shaped pit in sand and waits at the bottom for ants to fall in.
It flicks sand at prey to keep it sliding down, grabs it with curved jaws, and sucks out its body fluids. Larvae can live up to three years and survive months without food or water.
Would you have stepped into the trap? Comment below.
thumbnail_text: THE SAND TRAP NO ANT ESCAPES
first_comment: The larva has no mouth that opens and closes. It drinks its meals through its jaws. Gross or genius?
